# Dopamine agonists and apomorphine — facts

> Source-anchored units about Dopamine agonists and apomorphine: 11 across 3 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

## How it works

- [statement] The AAN recommends using the lowest effective dopamine-agonist dose and, when stopping treatment because of adverse effects, gradual dose reduction when possible with monitoring for dopamine agonist withdrawal syndrome. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] Both US apomorphine labels contraindicate concomitant use with ondansetron, listed among serotonin receptor antagonists, because profound hypotension and loss of consciousness have been reported. (medium confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/214056s005.pdf · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/021264s025lbl.pdf
- [statement] Apomorphine infusion has specific local tolerability burdens: the ONAPGO label warns of infusion-site reactions and infections and instructs daily site changes; it also warns that treatment can cause or worsen dyskinesia. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/214056s005.pdf · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The 2021 AAN guideline allows dopamine agonists as initial treatment in selected early-PD patients younger than 60 years who are at higher dyskinesia risk; it advises against their use for initial treatment in those older than 70 years or with preexisting cognitive impairment, excessive daytime sleepiness, or hallucinations. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] In the PROUD delayed-start trial, clinical and neuroimaging outcomes did not support a disease-modifying effect of pramipexole, consistent with the AAN guideline assessment of dopamine agonist trials. (medium confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23726851/ · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In the 12-week randomized TOLEDO trial, apomorphine infusion reduced daily OFF time by 2·47 hours versus 0·58 hours with placebo, a between-group difference of 1·89 hours (95% CI 0·62–3·16 hours favoring apomorphine); six apomorphine-treated participants withdrew because of treatment-related adverse events. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30055903/ · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For early PD, the AAN review found greater motor improvement with initial levodopa than with initial dopamine agonists, while initial agonists caused less dyskinesia during the first five years; severe or disabling dyskinesia was uncommon in that interval. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] The AAN found no strong evidence favoring ropinirole over pramipexole or extended-release over immediate-release pramipexole for early-PD motor efficacy; formulation, administration route, cost, and patient preferences should guide selection. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] Dopamine agonists require monitoring for daytime somnolence, sudden sleep onset, hallucinations, nausea, and orthostatic hypotension; these are also explicit apomorphine-label safety concerns. (medium confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8672433/ · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine · also: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/214056s005.pdf
- [statement] APOKYN prescribing information revised January 2025 describes subcutaneous apomorphine for acute, intermittent treatment of OFF episodes in advanced PD and requires the first dose under medical supervision. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2025/021264s025lbl.pdf · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
- [statement] ONAPGO prescribing information revised May 2026 describes subcutaneous infusion for motor fluctuations in adults with advanced PD; it explicitly states that ONAPGO is not substitutable for apomorphine products intended for intermittent use. (low confidence) — https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/214056s005.pdf · keywords: Dopamine agonists and apomorphine
